content.user_title: Analyze Equity Derivatives and Hybrid Securities
content.value_statement: Equity derivative analysis requires reliable contract terms, market data, and clear risk framing. This skill routes each request through a focused, evidence-based workflow.
actual_capabilities: Routes requests to a single-stock derivative or hybrid security workflow.
Identifies required contract terms, market data, objectives, and valuation dates.
Compares listed option structures based on payoff, Greeks, catalysts, and risk.
Decomposes convertibles and warrants into credit, equity, optionality, dilution, and liquidity drivers.
Builds price, volatility, time-decay, conversion, and exercise scenarios.
Reports assumptions, stale data notices, missing inputs, and instrument-specific risks.
limitations: Requires LLMQuant Data or user-provided market and contract data for current analysis.
Does not value instruments when essential term sheet fields are unavailable.
Does not fabricate option quotes, Greeks, borrow rates, or conversion terms.
Does not determine personal suitability without the user's mandate and constraints.

use_cases.title: Design a Single-Stock Options Trade
use_cases.description: Compare structures around a market view, catalyst, time horizon, maximum loss, liquidity, and volatility conditions.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Convertible Security
use_cases.description: Assess bond value, embedded optionality, conversion thresholds, call provisions, credit exposure, and dilution.

use_cases.title: Review Warrant Terms and Scenarios
use_cases.description: Examine strike, expiry, exercise style, redemption triggers, anti-dilution clauses, and outcomes across underlying prices.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Required Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to analyze {instrument} on {ticker}. List the contract terms and market data required before analysis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete input checklist

prompt_templates.title: Compare Option Structures
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare option structures for {ticker} given {market view}, {horizon}, {catalyst}, and {maximum loss}. Include payoff, Greeks, liquidity, and key risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate selection among listed option strategies

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Convertible or Warrant
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this {convertible or warrant} using the supplied terms and market data. Decompose value drivers and present threshold scenarios, dilution, and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test a Derivative Thesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Stress test {instrument} across price, volatility, time, credit, borrow, and event outcomes. Compare alternatives and explain when no derivative is justified.

output_examples.input: Compare a call spread and an outright call for a six-month bullish view with a defined loss limit.
output_examples.output: Derivative View: Moderately bullish. Best-Fit Structure: Call spread when implied volatility is expensive. Payoff: Capped upside with lower premium. Risks: Liquidity and catalyst timing.

output_examples.input: Assess a convertible bond using supplied coupon, maturity, conversion price, call terms, bond price, stock price, and volatility.
output_examples.output: Instrument Summary: Balanced credit and equity exposure. Valuation Drivers: Credit floor, conversion premium, volatility, and call risk. Scenarios: Below, near, and above conversion price.

best_practices: Provide the exact ticker, instrument type, objective, time horizon, and risk budget.
Include timestamped quotes, contract terms, volatility history, event dates, and liquidity data.
Review assumptions, missing inputs, payoff boundaries, and adverse scenarios before using the analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not request a contract recommendation without current option-chain or term-sheet data.
Do not treat convertibles or warrants as equivalent to common stock.
Do not ignore bid-ask spreads, liquidity, dilution, call provisions, credit risk, or borrow costs.

faq.question: Which instruments does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers listed single-stock options, structured payoffs, convertibles, warrants, rights, and other equity-linked hybrid securities.

faq.question: Does the skill provide current market data?
faq.answer: It relies on LLMQuant Data or user-provided data for prices, option chains, volatility, borrow, corporate actions, and security terms.

faq.question: Can it recommend a specific option contract?
faq.answer: It can compare contracts when current chains, Greeks, liquidity, objectives, and constraints are available. Otherwise, it states the missing inputs.

faq.question: How does it analyze convertibles?
faq.answer: It separates bond value, embedded option value, conversion terms, credit, dilution, call risk, liquidity, and price scenarios.

faq.question: What happens when contract terms are missing?
faq.answer: It lists the exact missing fields and avoids valuing the instrument or inventing terms.

faq.question: Is the output personal investment advice?
faq.answer: No. The workflow supports structured research and requires mandate and constraint details before discussing suitability.
